Definition.Name: Multi-team software delivery and release governance
Definition.Summary: Universal delivery template for planned software change with explicit intake, architecture, implementation, QA, security, release, deployment, and retrospective governance aligned to the current process-module graph model.
Definition.ValueStatement: Delivers customer-visible or internal software change through a controllable sequence that keeps scope, evidence, dependencies, artifact inputs, and release authority explicit.
Definition.InterfaceContractSummary: Feature delivery crosses process authoring, workspace, billing, and release-management boundaries and therefore needs explicit design, validation, and release gates.
Definition.GovernanceNotes: No role or approval decision may be collapsed into an implicit chat or tribal handoff; every trust-sensitive transition needs explicit accountability, evidence, dependency mapping, and artifact-input traceability.
Definition.ChangeSummary: Refreshed for the current process architecture so multi-parent joins, artifact inputs, and decision-role semantics are first-class instead of simulated through legacy fields only.
Definition.GovernancePolicySummary: Release readiness requires architecture proof, QA evidence, security posture, rollback readiness, and explicit residual-risk ownership.
Definition.ConstitutionRuleSummary: Role contracts, decision rights, and source-of-truth ownership outlive the specific person or agent assigned at runtime.
Definition.OperatingModeSummary: Governed live execution is allowed only after explicit quality, security, and release gates succeed.
Definition.SimulationReadinessSummary: This scenario is intentionally rich enough for simulation, canvas authoring, analytics, and large-screen browser walkthroughs.

Roles.Purpose: Convert business intent into an explicit delivery contract with clear acceptance boundaries and prioritized value trade-offs.
Roles.StaffingIntent: One accountable human decision-maker who can clarify scope, decide priority, accept delivered outcomes, and absorb stakeholder escalation without routing every decision through engineering.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Outcome and acceptance owner for value, scope, sequencing, and release acceptance.

Roles.Purpose: Keep the process executable by turning desired outcomes into a feasible, staffed, time-aware delivery path with explicit escalation triggers.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A senior delivery-side coordinator with enough authority to challenge unrealistic dates, surface hidden dependencies, and keep multiple roles synchronized.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Flow owner for sequencing, staffing realism, dependency control, and execution escalation.

Roles.Purpose: Protect maintainability and operability by reviewing design options, target architecture fit, and downstream integration impact before costly implementation commitment.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A senior technical authority who can reason across components, environments, data boundaries, and operational consequences.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Architecture authority for system boundaries, irreversible decisions, and cross-domain technical coherence.

Roles.Purpose: Own the change set and keep implementation evidence aligned with the approved architecture and release boundary.
Roles.StaffingIntent: Build-capable engineering owner for the working change set and adjacent test evidence.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Implementation owner for code, tests, migration notes, and executable delivery proof.

Roles.Purpose: Challenge whether the delivered change is proven enough for its risk profile and make test evidence decision-ready for release governance.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A senior test leader able to shape strategy, select evidence depth, and identify where automation is not enough.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Quality owner for coverage depth, evidence quality, and release confidence.

Roles.Purpose: Ensure changes touching trust boundaries, sensitive data, dependencies, or operational attack surface are reviewed proportionally and documented defensibly.
Roles.StaffingIntent: A senior security practitioner who can translate security risk into concrete engineering and governance decisions.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Security gate owner for threat assessment, exception handling, and trust-boundary decisions.

Roles.Purpose: Coordinate go-live preparation and keep rollback and telemetry watch ownership explicit before and during release execution.
Roles.StaffingIntent: Operational owner for production execution, release windows, and rollback decisions.
Roles.SnapshotSummary: Operational owner for rollout control, rollback readiness, and telemetry review.

Steps.Title: Clarify scope and release boundary
Steps.Subtitle: Value framing and no-go constraints
Steps.Notes: Capture the commercial ask, tenant impact, release deadline, known dependencies, and explicit exclusions before engineering commits.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Feature request, tenant-impact notes, target release window, and customer-facing constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Decision-ready scope packet with acceptance boundary and dependency map.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Intake notes, acceptance criteria, known exclusions, and unresolved dependency register.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Product owner can refine the ask but cannot waive architecture, data, or release-governance requirements.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Escalate immediately when timeline pressure conflicts with data-safety or release constraints.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: If the original product owner changes, ownership transfers to the next accountable value owner without changing the process contract.
Delivery review remains explicit even if staffing changes mid-stream.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Scope boundary packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable during architecture review, implementation planning, and future scope-drift analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture no-go constraints, tenant impact, and acceptance boundary in typed form.

Steps.Title: Review architecture and canonical-model impact
Steps.Subtitle: Cross-module and source-of-truth decision
Steps.Notes: Validate process/workspace/billing seams, canonical model implications, migration ownership, and integration boundaries before implementation starts.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Scope packet, touched modules, data-flow map, and integration concerns.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved architecture path with explicit trade-offs and rejected alternatives.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Architecture notes, canonical-model decision, and source-of-truth rationale.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Architecture authority recommends the path; delivery manager remains accountable for choosing the approved option.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not continue while source-of-truth ownership or migration responsibility remains ambiguous.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Architecture authority may be reassigned between vetted humans or approved architecture agents.
Implementation owner must confirm the design is buildable before approval.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Architecture decision record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for implementation, review, and later forensic replay.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture selected option, rejected options, source-of-truth choice, and migration ownership.

Steps.Title: Implement feature, tests, and migration notes
Steps.Subtitle: Code, tests, and reviewable proof
Steps.Notes: Produce the change set, migration guidance, and targeted validation without losing traceability to the approved design.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Approved architecture path, scope packet, and unresolved technical questions.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Review-ready implementation with tests, migration notes, and rollout checklist inputs.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Change set, test outputs, migration steps, and touched-surface inventory.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Lead engineer can implement but cannot silently alter the approved architecture or reduce proof depth.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Pause when migration impact, performance risk, or dependency scope grows beyond the approved path.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Engineering ownership moves between qualified engineers without changing the role contract.
Value owner reviews only acceptance drift, not technical implementation details.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Implementation change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for peer review, release approval, and later defect forensics.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must be linked to tests, migration notes, and touched-surface inventory.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Migration and rollout preparation checklist
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release rehearsal and rollback planning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name data changes, operational preconditions, and rollback steps.

Steps.Title: Complete peer review and integration readiness
Steps.Subtitle: Design and implementation challenge
Steps.Notes: Review the change set against the approved design, integration consequences, and release assumptions.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Implementation package, architecture decision record, and changed-surface inventory.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Peer-reviewed change set with explicit residual risk and follow-up items.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Review notes, unresolved issues list, and approved follow-up actions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Reviewers may block unsafe merge or release progression until the change set satisfies design and evidence expectations.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not downgrade architecture, data, or migration concerns to cosmetic comments.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Implementation owner remains attached until review comments are addressed.
Architectural review remains explicit when cross-module consequences exist.
QA participates when changed surface suggests regression risk.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Peer review note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for QA, security, and release governance.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture accepted issues, rejected concerns, and explicit residual risk.

Steps.Title: Run QA validation and browser proof
Steps.Subtitle: Regression, UX, and quality evidence
Steps.Notes: Execute targeted regression, browser proof, and defect triage against the reviewed implementation package.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Peer-reviewed change set, changed-surface inventory, and release-scope assumptions.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Targeted QA result with screenshots, regressions, and explicit residual quality risk.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Regression logs, browser proof, screenshots, and defect notes.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: QA lead may block release progression when evidence is too thin for the risk profile.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not let schedule pressure replace proof with verbal confidence.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: QA ownership may move across qualified reviewers without collapsing the gate.
Implementation owner reviews failures and fixes before release approval.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Regression evidence pack
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release approval, incident review, and later regression comparison.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name changed flows, assertion depth, screenshots, and unresolved risks.

Steps.Title: Perform security and data-handling review
Steps.Subtitle: Tenant data, secrets, and exception posture
Steps.Notes: Review tenant-data handling, secrets, boundary changes, and policy exceptions before release approval.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Peer-reviewed package, changed-surface inventory, and data-handling notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Security outcome with explicit approval, block, or exception rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Security review notes, exception rationale, and approved controls.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Security reviewer owns the sign-off for tenant-data and policy exceptions.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block release when data-handling review capacity is missing or exception rationale is incomplete.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Security approval remains attached to the role even if the reviewer changes.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Security exception assessment
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release governance, audit, and post-incident review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture controls, residual risk owner, and approval or block rationale.

Steps.Title: Approve release readiness
Steps.Subtitle: Go / no-go board decision
Steps.Notes: Approve or reject release using QA proof, security posture, rollback readiness, and support coverage.
Steps.InputContractSummary: QA evidence, security outcome, rollback plan, and support ownership.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved or rejected release readiness with accountable rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Approval note, residual risk register, and rollback ownership record.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Delivery manager owns the decision and cannot waive missing proof or missing rollback readiness silently.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Reject release when security review, rollback ownership, or support readiness remains incomplete.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Release approval belongs to the accountable delivery manager role, not to whichever person attended a meeting.
Operational release owner reviews rollback and support readiness before the board decision.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Release approval record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for audit, release replay, and governance tuning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name the approver, residual risk owner, rollback trigger, and release timing conditions.

Steps.Title: Execute controlled release rollout
Steps.Subtitle: Live execution and first-hour telemetry watch
Steps.Notes: Deploy the approved change inside the controlled release window while telemetry and rollback readiness remain actively managed.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Approved release record, deployment package, rollback plan, and telemetry watch points.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Executed rollout with explicit telemetry outcome, rollback status, and live-watch notes.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Operator notes, telemetry checkpoints, and any rollback invocation or release halt.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Release manager may execute only inside the approved window and rollback-trigger boundaries.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Trigger halt or rollback immediately when telemetry, tenant impact, or operational constraints breach the approved threshold.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Execution ownership remains with the release-manager role until rollout completes or fails.
Implementation owner stays available for rapid corrective interpretation during rollout.
Governance owner reviews telemetry and escalation timing during the release window.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Deployment and telemetry watch log
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for incident replay and release retrospectives.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture release timing, telemetry checkpoints, and any halt or rollback decision.

Steps.Title: Capture post-release learning and corrective actions
Steps.Subtitle: Forensic replay and systemic follow-up
Steps.Notes: Turn the release outcome into explicit learning about design, QA, operations, and process behavior.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Rollout outcome, telemetry record, support observations, and any release incident notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Post-release learning review with corrective actions and simulation updates.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Timeline, contributing factors, missing controls, and next corrective actions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Delivery manager owns follow-up assignment while architecture and release roles retain responsibility for their own control gaps.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close the process while critical corrective actions remain unnamed or unowned.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Follow-up ownership remains explicit until corrective actions have accountable owners.
Architecture role reviews systemic design findings rather than only local defects.
Release role reviews telemetry and rollback-control lessons.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Post-release learning review
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for process improvement and future simulation baselines.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture orchestration-quality observations, not only technical defects.

Warnings: Detailed sidecar metadata remains in the process-template pack files.
